# Psalm 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-psalm of-David, when-he-fled from-before Absalom his-son.

**2** YHWH, how-many [are] my-adversaries! Many [are] rising against-me.

**3** Many [are] saying of-my-soul, 'There-is-no salvation for-him in-God.' Selah.

**4** But-You, YHWH, [are] a-shield about-me, my-glory and-the-One-lifting my-head.

**5** [With] my-voice to YHWH I-cry-out, and-He-answers-me from-His-holy mountain. Selah.

**6** I lay-down and-I-slept; I-awoke, for YHWH sustains-me.

**7** I-will-not fear the-myriads of-people who all-around have-set [themselves] against-me.

**8** Arise, YHWH! Save-me, my-God! For You-have-struck all my-enemies [on the] cheek; the-teeth of-the-wicked You-have-broken.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **3:1**: The superscription ties this psalm to 2 Samuel 15-17 — David's flight from Absalom's coup.

- **3:3**: Selah — meaning uncertain. Possibly a liturgical pause, a musical interlude, or a signal to raise the voice.

— EMET
